Description

On late endosomes a small scaffold holds MEK1 and ERK1. MP1 (MEK partner 1, LAMTOR3) binds MEK1 and ERK1, but not MEK2 or ERK2, and helps their activation [1]. MP1 pairs with p14 (LAMTOR2), which sits on the cytoplasmic face of late endosomes, and the p14-MP1 complex can hold ERK and MEK [2]. The two form a tight heterodimer whose free surfaces are the docking sites for ERK1 and MEK1 [3]. The lipid raft protein p18 (LAMTOR1) anchors the p14-MP1 pair to late endosomes, and without p18 the pair leaves them and MEK-ERK activity falls [4]. Lowering MP1 or p14 impairs signal transmission [5], and in mice the p14-MP1-MEK1 complex controls late endosomal traffic and cell proliferation in the skin [6]. The same three proteins also form the Ragulator, which brings the Rag GTPases and mTORC1 to lysosomes [7].
